tier1.text: Each postcentral gyrus processes touch, pressure, tickle, pain, itch and vibration. The postcentral gyrus is a ridge in the parietal lobe, a region at the top of the brain. This ridge is where these sensations are first processed and consciously felt. Each postcentral gyrus receives its sensations from the opposite side of the body.

sentences.text: Each postcentral gyrus processes touch, pressure, tickle, pain, itch and vibration.

quotes.quote: Posterior to the central sulcus is the postcentral gyrus, the primary somatosensory cortex, which is identified as Brodmann’s areas 1, 2, and 3. All of the tactile senses are processed in this area, including touch, pressure, tickle, pain, itch, and vibration
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: postcentral gyrus: ridge just posterior to the central sulcus, in the parietal lobe, where somatosensory processing initially takes place in the cerebrum

sentences.text: This ridge is where these sensations are first processed and consciously felt.

quotes.quote: The third neuron in the system projects its axons to the postcentral gyrus of the cerebral cortex, where somatosensory stimuli are initially processed and the conscious perception of the stimulus occurs.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Each postcentral gyrus receives its sensations from the opposite side of the body.

quotes.quote: Motor commands from the precentral gyrus control the opposite side of the body, whereas sensory information processed by the postcentral gyrus is received from the opposite side of the body.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
